name: Limpopo flood at Chokwe, Mozambique
claim: NISAR radar shows about 150 km² of land around Chokwe newly under open water on 17 Jan 2026, compared with 24 Dec 2025.

measured.estimate_basis: open water is a class of radar brightness (HH below a threshold), not a survey

method.water_threshold_rule: Otsu (1979) on the smoothed HH of the flood pass, inside -22 to -12 dB
method.new_water_rule: HH below the threshold on the later pass, not below it on the earlier pass, and at least 3 dB darker (two-pass form of the detect.py water rule)
method.coherence_classes: new water and unchanged land between the two passes of the flood pair, on GUNW cells of 80 m covered at least to pure_cell_share by one class; the control pair is read on the same cells
method.control_pair: the same rule and threshold on two passes before the flood, 12 and 24 Dec 2025
method.control_reverse_pair: the same rule from 24 Dec back to 12 Dec, both before the flood, with the same window-wide darkening (-1.5 dB) as 24 Dec to 5 Jan (-1.4 dB)
method.control_to_rising_pair: the same rule from 12 Dec to 5 Jan, two passes with the same window-wide brightness
method.median_shift_removed: the window median of the dB change between the two passes is added to the earlier pass before the rule runs
method.hv_rule: the same two-pass rule on the smoothed HV, with an Otsu threshold of the flood pass HV inside hv_otsu_range_db (-21.8 dB)

gunw.coherence_ramp: radar-lo at 0 to radar-hi at 1, linear

caveats.text: All products are BETA releases (CRID X05010).
The flood is seen on one pass, 17 Jan 2026; ASF lists no NISAR pass of any track over Chokwe from then until 22 Jun 2026.
Flooded shrubs and crops can turn brighter at L-band instead of darker, so open water is a lower bound of the flooded area.
Water standing in irrigated fields counts as open water; radar brightness alone cannot tell irrigation water from flood water.
On 5 Jan land that stayed dry was 1.3 dB darker in HH than on 24 Dec.

The water reached this window between 5 and 17 Jan. The 7.6 km² the rule finds by 5 Jan comes from that pass being darker overall: the same rule finds 7.5 km² from 24 Dec back to 12 Dec, both before the flood, and 0.4 km² by 5 Jan once the darkening is removed.

context.source: NASA Earth Observatory, Image of the Day, 27 Jan 2026, 'Floods Inundate Southern Mozambique'
facts: at least 30,000 homes destroyed or damaged
at least 180,000 ha of crops flooded

context.source: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio, page 5661, 6 Aug 2026, 'NISAR Reveals Major Flooding In Mozambique'
facts: compares NISAR GCOV images of 5 and 17 Jan 2026 over Chokwe and Macia
false colour with HH red, HV green and the ratio of the two bands blue
